purpose: Canonical machine-readable status for capabilities whose presence affects architecture claims. This file records documentation truth; it does not authorize implementation or lab changes.

status_vocabulary.accepted: Installed or configured on the named boundary and supported by current acceptance evidence.
status_vocabulary.installed-not-accepted: Present, but the named access or operating boundary has not completed acceptance.
status_vocabulary.requires-revalidation: An older presence claim exists, but it is not canonical until revalidated.
status_vocabulary.provisioned-only: Compute or routing may exist, but the product is not installed.
status_vocabulary.not-installed: The capability is part of target design only.
status_vocabulary.target-only: A future architecture option with no accepted runtime target.
status_vocabulary.partial: Only the explicitly named sub-boundaries are accepted.

harbor.accepted_boundary: Harbor 2.15.0 on harbor.example.com; ten product containers healthy; native HTTPS and health API return successful results.
harbor.unaccepted_boundary: None on the accepted native endpoint; the retired shared compatibility route is absent.
harbor.design_rule: Documentation may describe Harbor as installed and healthy only at harbor.example.com.

vault.accepted_boundary: The product-local frontend at vault.example.com is reachable.
vault.unaccepted_boundary: The latest /v1/sys/health probe returned HTTP 503 for sealed/standby state; unsealed operation is not currently accepted.
vault.design_rule: Application secret delivery remains a separate design and acceptance concern; Vault presence does not imply healthy unsealed operation or External Secrets Operator.

keycloak.design_rule: Describe Keycloak and OIDC integration as planned or conditional until revalidation is accepted.

artifactory.design_rule: Do not claim artifact publication or product operation.

sonarqube.design_rule: Do not claim a live quality-gate service.

splunk.design_rule: Keep Splunk as a target comparison product; do not describe it as operating.

argocd.design_rule: GitOps is a target operating model. Jenkins remains the accepted Kubernetes release owner until a separately approved bootstrap and ownership handoff completes.

external-secrets-operator.design_rule: Describe the Kubernetes secret-store integration as a planned contract, not current behavior.

kubernetes-ingress.accepted_boundary: Single-replica ClusterIP-only ingress-nginx with worker-local NGINX access.
kubernetes-ingress.design_rule: Do not imply a cloud load balancer, MetalLB or public ingress.

longhorn.accepted_boundary: Longhorn 1.12.0 V1 on the three worker /data/longhorn paths with a healthy three-replica acceptance volume.
longhorn.design_rule: Off-cluster backup and disaster recovery remain separate design decisions.

internal-tls.accepted_boundary: Harbor native HTTPS and the documented Vault HTTPS path.
internal-tls.unaccepted_boundary: Most user-facing lab endpoints remain HTTP; enterprise-wide certificate distribution and TLS migration are not accepted.
internal-tls.design_rule: Never summarize TLS as either fully installed or entirely absent; name the endpoint-specific boundary.

public-cloud.design_rule: AWS, Azure, GCP, EKS, AKS and GKE are governed extension designs, not current runtime claims.

business-applications.accepted_boundary: Podinfo is registered and documented but is not deployed. No care-delivery or payer application repository is registered.
business-applications.design_rule: Do not invent application projects or application-to-application contracts. Record them only after real names, repositories and owners are supplied.
